title: Counting inversions: all pairs vs merge sort
problem_statement: Given a sequence a_1..a_n, count the pairs i < j with a_i > a_j.

algorithms.name: all pairs
algorithms.pseudocode: count pairs i < j with a_i > a_j

algorithms.name: merge-sort counting
algorithms.idea: Sort recursively and count cross inversions while merging: a right-half element placed before the remaining left-half elements is inverted with each of them.
algorithms.correctness: Every inversion lies within the left half, within the right half, or across; cross inversions are counted exactly once during the merge (CLRS Problem 2-4).

shape.note: count depends on the drawn instance; kept so the record says why the diagnostic cannot decide

relationship: Theta(n^2) -> Theta(n log n) by divide and conquer. Faster algorithms exist in the word-RAM model (O(n sqrt(log n)), Chan & Pătraşcu 2010).

sources.authors: Cormen, T. H.; Leiserson, C. E.; Rivest, R. L.; Stein, C.
sources.title: Introduction to Algorithms (3rd ed.)

sources.note: O(n sqrt(log n)) in the word RAM.

verification.method: V1: both agree with each other and with an independent Fenwick-tree oracle on random sequences with duplicates, n = 0..500. V2 (since 2026-10-07, research/2026-10-07b_count_based_v2.md): the measured quantity is the exact number of ELEMENT COMPARISONS made by the unchanged implementations, counted by an instrumented element type (CountingKey in harness.py) wrapped around the values of generate() (uniform on [0, n], the same seeded inputs the earlier timing fit used). All pairs: exactly n(n-1)/2 at n = 250, 500, 750, 1000, 1500, 2000; alpha = 1.001 against n^2. Merge-sort counting, 1 sample (the 3-sample spread was at most 0.11% of the count) at n = 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000, 64000: 19421, 42827, 93679, 203327, 438368, 941126 comparisons = n log2 n - c n with c = 1.255 to 1.267, each within the merge bounds sum of min(left, right) <= C <= sum of (left + right - 1), which hold for every input (each step of the merge loop makes one comparison and outputs one element, and the loop stops as soon as one run is exhausted, so merging runs of lengths left, right >= 1 takes at least min(left, right) and at most left + right - 1 comparisons); alpha = 1.010 against n log n, the excess coming from the -c n term. Tolerance 0.03: exact counts carry no timing noise, so the band only covers lower-order terms (largest |alpha - 1| here 0.010) and stays below half the distance to the nearest rival. Rivals that must NOT fit, all rejected: all pairs against n log n (alpha = 1.735) and n^2 log n (0.930); merge-sort counting against n (1.119), n log^2 n (0.920) and n^2 (0.560). The log factor is therefore resolved for both (validator diagnostic, RESEARCH_LOG RL-048). experiments/2026-10-07b_count_v2_inversions_lis.py reproduces every count above.

caveats: V2 counts element comparisons, not every machine operation; with exact counts the log factor IS resolved (the rivals n and n*log(n)^2 are rejected; RL-057). The earlier timing fit could not resolve it (RL-048).
